guide.title: Stratford, Connecticut: Birthplace of the American Helicopter
guide.intro: Stratford was settled in 1639 by Rev. Adam Blakeman and William Beardsley with a group of families, and by April 13, 1643 the growing settlement was known as Stratford, honoring Stratford-upon-Avon; the Paugussett had called the place Cupheag. Stratford's original colonial land grant was far larger than today's town, including territory that later became Trumbull, Shelton, Monroe and part of Bridgeport. Oystering and shipbuilding were the early industries, later giving way to manufacturing. Stratford is recognized as the birthplace of the American helicopter industry: Igor Sikorsky's VS-300, the world's first practical helicopter, flew here on September 14, 1939, and every Marine One presidential helicopter has been built in Stratford since 1957. Stratford's railroad station opened December 25, 1848; the same depot building now also houses the National Helicopter Museum.

sections.heading: Birthplace of the American helicopter
sections.body: Igor Sikorsky's tethered September 14, 1939 flight of the VS-300 in Stratford is credited as the world's first practical helicopter; the aircraft's first free flight followed on May 13, 1940. Every Marine One presidential helicopter has been manufactured in Stratford since 1957, continuing Sikorsky's legacy. The American Shakespeare Theatre, an 1,100-seat house that opened in 1955 and drew major stage actors, ceased operations in the mid-1980s and burned down in 2019 — it no longer hosts performances. Two Roads Brewing Company, one of Connecticut's largest craft breweries, anchors a multi-venue campus on Stratford Avenue that also includes a separate experimental brewhouse and a food hall.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Stratford sits on Long Island Sound between Bridgeport and Milford, reached by car on I-95, US Route 1 or the Merritt Parkway. Metro-North's New Haven Line stops at Stratford station, 2480 Main Street, with 294 parking spaces; adjacent stations are Bridgeport toward Grand Central and Milford toward New Haven. Shore Line East, as of 2026, runs only between New Haven and New London and does not stop in Stratford. Amtrak does not stop at Stratford either — the nearest Amtrak service is at Bridgeport and New Haven on the Northeast Corridor.

faq.question: How do I get to Stratford?
faq.answer: By car on I-95, US Route 1 or the Merritt Parkway, or by train — Metro-North's New Haven Line stops at Stratford station, 2480 Main Street, between Bridgeport and Milford.

faq.question: Is there Amtrak or Shore Line East service in Stratford?
faq.answer: No. Amtrak does not stop in Stratford (nearest is Bridgeport or New Haven), and Shore Line East runs only between New Haven and New London as of 2026.

faq.question: What is the National Helicopter Museum?
faq.answer: A free museum inside Stratford's historic 1848 railroad depot, with a model of the town's 1939 first helicopter flight and an actual Sikorsky S-76 cockpit. Open Wednesday-Sunday, 1-4 p.m., Memorial Day through mid-October.

faq.question: Is there a hotel in Stratford?
faq.answer: No lodging inside Stratford could be verified. The nearest confirmed option is the Delamar Southport, about a dozen miles west.

places.name: Boothe Memorial Park & Museum
places.summary: A 32-acre former Boothe family homestead (1663-1949) with an eccentric collection of historic structures, rose and wedding gardens, and farm-equipment and trolley displays. Free admission. Grounds open daily 9 a.m.-5 p.m.; museum buildings open June 1-October 1, Tue-Fri 11 a.m.-1 p.m., Sun 1-4 p.m.

places.name: Stratford Historical Society — Captain David Judson House & Catharine B. Mitchell Museum
places.summary: Interprets Stratford's colonial past through the Captain David Judson House, the Catharine B. Mitchell Museum and the Beach Family Carriage House. Open Tuesdays and Fridays, 10 a.m.-2 p.m., or by appointment. Phone (203) 378-0630.

places.name: Great Meadows Marsh Unit, Stewart B. McKinney National Wildlife Refuge
places.summary: The Stratford unit of the Stewart B. McKinney National Wildlife Refuge, one of ten units spread across 70 miles of Connecticut coastline and designated an Important Bird Area. Stay on established trails and viewing platforms. Visitor services (860) 399-2513 ext. 8134.

places.name: Two Roads Brewing Company
places.summary: One of Connecticut's largest and best-known craft breweries, anchoring a multi-venue campus on Stratford Avenue. Phone (203) 335-2010.

places.name: Two Roads Food Hall + Bar
places.summary: Kiosk-and-counter food hall on the Two Roads campus, with a drink list of Two Roads beers, ready-to-drink cocktails and local spirits. Hours Wed-Thu 4-9 p.m., Fri-Sat noon-9 p.m., Sun noon-6 p.m. Phone (203) 290-4731.

places.name: Area Two Experimental Brewing
places.summary: Two Roads' separate experimental brewhouse and taproom on the same Stratford Avenue campus. Shares the (203) 335-2010 line.

places.name: Duchess Restaurant
places.summary: Stratford outpost of Duchess, a Connecticut-owned family burger-and-diner group with 11 locations concentrated in the Bridgeport/Fairfield County area. Phone (203) 378-2141.
